To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a semantic information-retrival method for identifying and ordering likely candidate services based on the provided service-description is effective and efficient; and (2) the use of structural similarity assessment for refining a set of likely candidates is effective, efficient, and robust.

(a) our semantic structure-matching method can be successfully used to assess the similarity among WSDL files, and (b) the combination of the two similarity-assessment methods (i.e., the information-retrieval and semantic-structure matching) can be used to effectively identify the most similar web service among a large set of available services.
the combination of the two methods, i.e., information retrieval and structure matching, is the best performing approach for assessing the similarity of web-services descriptions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the semantic-structure matching method is more effective than semantic matching of service identifiers in the context of service discovery, and that it is more robust to errors in the input service specifications.

the semantic structure-matching approach is the most effective in terms of precision and recall, and that the combination of the two methods is the most effective when both precision and recall are taken into consideration.
the methods we have developed are effective in assessing service similarity, and that they can be used to support the discovery and composition of web services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to assess service similarity with a precision of about 90% at a recall of 50% (or 60% at a recall level of 30%).
the semantic structure-matching approach is the best approach to assess the similarity between two web-services specifications.
the combination of semantic information-retrieving and semantic structure-matching methods is effective in assessing the semantic similarity of web services.
